paragraphs.title: Hananiah’s Prophecy of Breaking Babylon’s Yoke and Returning the Exiles

answers: In the house of the LORD
In the king’s palace
At the city gate
easy.explanation: Hananiah spoke to Jeremiah in the house of the LORD, before the priests and all the people.
easy.q: Where did Hananiah speak his prophecy?

answers: The yoke of the king of Egypt
The yoke of the king of Babylon
The yoke of the king of Assyria
easy.explanation: Hananiah declared, “I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.”
easy.q: What did Hananiah say had been broken?

answers: Within one month
Within one year
Within two full years
easy.explanation: Hananiah said the vessels and captives would be brought back within two full years.
easy.q: Within how long did Hananiah say the promised events would happen?

answers: The vessels of the LORD’s house, Jeconiah, and all the captives of Judah
Only the silver and gold vessels
Only the priests and the Temple vessels
medium.explanation: He promised the return of the Temple vessels, Jeconiah, and all the captives of Judah.
medium.q: What did Hananiah promise would be brought back from Babylon?

answers: Before Jeremiah alone
Before the priests and all the people
Before the king of Babylon
medium.explanation: Hananiah spoke in the house of the LORD in the presence of the priests and all the people.
medium.q: Before whom did Hananiah make his announcement?

answers: A musical instrument
A royal garment
Submission to authority and bondage
medium.explanation: The yoke represents the rule and bondage imposed by the king of Babylon.
medium.q: What does the word “yoke” represent in Hananiah’s prophecy?

answers: It concerned the restoration of sacred things that had been taken away
It proved that Hananiah was a priest
It described the construction of the Temple
challenge.explanation: The return of the vessels represented the restoration of what had been taken from the LORD’s house.
challenge.q: Why would the return of the vessels of the LORD’s house strengthen Hananiah’s message?

answers: Both describe Babylon becoming stronger
Both describe release from Babylonian rule
They are unrelated in the prophecy
challenge.explanation: Breaking the yoke and returning the captives together picture the end of Babylonian control.
challenge.q: What connection does Hananiah make between breaking the yoke and returning the captives?

answers: It was spoken secretly
It was spoken only after his death
It was spoken publicly in the LORD’s name
challenge.explanation: Hananiah spoke publicly in the house of the LORD before the priests and the people, claiming to speak for the LORD.
challenge.q: What was distinctive about the setting of Hananiah’s prophecy?

paragraphs.title: Jeremiah’s Response and the Test of Prophecy

answers: He said, “Amen: the LORD do so”
He immediately ran away
He remained silent
easy.explanation: Jeremiah initially expressed the hope that Hananiah’s good prophecy would come to pass.
easy.q: How did Jeremiah first respond to Hananiah’s words?

answers: The vessels of the LORD’s house and all the captives
The army of Babylon
Many foreign kingdoms
easy.explanation: Jeremiah hoped for the return of the vessels and everything carried away captive from Babylon.
easy.q: What did Jeremiah hope would be brought back?

answers: By the number of people listening
By whether his word came to pass
By his age
easy.explanation: The prophet would be known as truly sent by the LORD when his word came to pass.
easy.q: How would a prophet who prophesied peace be known?

answers: War, evil, and pestilence
Trade and building
Feasts only
medium.explanation: Jeremiah mentioned prophecies concerning war, evil, and pestilence.
medium.q: What subjects did Jeremiah say earlier prophets had prophesied about?

answers: A prophecy of peace had to be tested by its fulfillment
Hananiah had not spoken in the house of the LORD
Jeremiah had not heard Hananiah’s words
medium.explanation: Jeremiah said that a prophet of peace would be known when the prophecy came to pass.
medium.q: Why did Jeremiah not immediately declare Hananiah a true prophet?

answers: The prophet’s message or prediction
An object in the Temple
An argument between people
medium.explanation: Here, “word” refers to the prophetic message and its fulfillment.
medium.q: In the phrase “when the word of the prophet shall come to pass,” what does “word” mean?

answers: A prophecy of peace does not need to be fulfilled
A prophecy of calamity may warn of trouble, while a prophecy of peace is tested by fulfillment
There is no difference between them
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah explains that a prophet of peace must be shown true when the promised peace comes to pass.
challenge.q: What distinction does Jeremiah make between prophecies of calamity and a prophecy of peace?

answers: Jeremiah expressed hope but still pointed to the test of fulfillment
Jeremiah claimed that Hananiah was a king
Jeremiah said the captives would never return
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah hoped Hananiah’s words were true, but he emphasized that fulfillment would reveal the truth.
challenge.q: Why was Jeremiah’s “Amen” not absolute proof that he believed Hananiah was sent by the LORD?

answers: The stated time does not matter
The promise should be tested by whether it happens as declared
Every good promise must be true
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah connects the identification of a true prophet with the fulfillment of the stated promise.
challenge.q: What principle can be drawn from Jeremiah’s words about a prophet who promises good things at a specific time?

paragraphs.title: The Broken Yoke and the Intensified Burden

answers: He broke it
He hid it
He gave it to the king
easy.explanation: Hananiah took the yoke from Jeremiah’s neck and broke it.
easy.q: What did Hananiah do to the yoke on Jeremiah’s neck?

answers: That Babylon’s yoke would be broken within two full years
That Jeremiah would become king
That the Temple would immediately be destroyed
easy.explanation: Hananiah declared that the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar would be broken within two full years.
easy.q: What did Hananiah announce after breaking the yoke?

answers: Silver yokes
Iron yokes
Gold yokes
easy.explanation: The LORD declared that the wooden yokes would be replaced with yokes of iron.

answers: A stronger and harsher burden
Freedom for all nations
The building of the Temple
medium.explanation: The iron yokes represent a stronger form of bondage under Nebuchadnezzar.
medium.q: What do the iron yokes represent in the passage?

answers: That Babylon’s yoke would be removed
That Jeremiah had authority over Babylon
That the people stopped listening to prophets
medium.explanation: The action illustrated Hananiah’s claim that Babylon’s yoke would be broken.
medium.q: What message did Hananiah’s breaking of the wooden yoke illustrate?

answers: A wooden bar placed on the neck for control or labor
A vessel used in the Temple
A prophetic writing
medium.explanation: A yoke is a bar placed on the neck, symbolizing service or subjection.
medium.q: What is a yoke in the phrase “yokes of wood”?

answers: From supposed freedom to a harsher burden
From a harsh burden to immediate peace
From war to the building of the Temple
challenge.explanation: Hananiah portrayed freedom from Babylon, but the LORD announced an iron yoke, signifying a more severe burden.
challenge.q: How does the message change between Hananiah’s action and the LORD’s word afterward?

answers: To show the broad extent of authority given to Nebuchadnezzar
To describe the work of the priests
To announce that every nation would return to Judah
challenge.explanation: The mention of nations and beasts shows the wide scope of Nebuchadnezzar’s rule.
challenge.q: Why are both the nations and the beasts of the field mentioned in the LORD’s message?

answers: The personal yoke illustrates the wider subjection of the nations
There is no connection between the two yokes
The yoke represents only the Temple vessels
challenge.explanation: The yoke on Jeremiah served as a visible illustration of the bondage that would come upon the nations.
challenge.q: What is the symbolic connection between the yoke on Jeremiah’s neck and the yoke placed on the nations?

answers: The LORD had not sent him
He was sent by the king of Babylon
He was the high priest
easy.explanation: Jeremiah told Hananiah, “The LORD hath not sent thee.”
easy.q: What did Jeremiah declare about Hananiah’s calling?

answers: A lie
A new altar
War against Egypt
easy.explanation: Jeremiah said that Hananiah made the people trust in a lie.
easy.q: What did Jeremiah say Hananiah had caused the people to trust in?

answers: The following year
The same year, in the seventh month
Two years later, in the fifth month
easy.explanation: The passage states that Hananiah died the same year in the seventh month.

answers: Because he had taught rebellion against the LORD
Because he had only broken the wooden yoke
Because he had spoken in the house of the LORD
medium.explanation: The LORD said Hananiah would die because he had taught rebellion against the LORD.
medium.q: Why was Hananiah sentenced to die that year?

answers: It showed that Hananiah’s prediction did not come to pass
Hananiah withdrew his prophecy
Jeremiah declared that every good prophecy was false
medium.explanation: Hananiah promised a change within two years, but he died that same year.
medium.q: How does Hananiah’s death relate to Jeremiah’s test of prophecy?

answers: Resistance or disobedience against God
Quiet speech
A joyful announcement
medium.explanation: In this context, rebellion means opposition and disobedience toward the LORD.
medium.q: What does “rebellion” mean in the statement that Hananiah taught rebellion against the LORD?

answers: Hananiah died the same year, before the two full years had passed
Hananiah spoke in the fifth month
Jeremiah went his way
challenge.explanation: Hananiah promised change within two years, but he died before that period ended.
challenge.q: What time detail most clearly emphasizes the failure of Hananiah’s prophecy?

answers: His death underscores the seriousness of speaking falsely in the LORD’s name
His death proves Hananiah was a true prophet
There is no connection between his calling and his death
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah said Hananiah was not sent by the LORD, and the passage records his death that same year.
challenge.q: How do Jeremiah’s words about Hananiah’s calling connect with Hananiah’s death?

answers: Hananiah promised quick relief, but the ending confirms the rejection of his message
Hananiah promised war, but the people received peace
Hananiah remained silent, but Jeremiah spoke
challenge.explanation: Hananiah promised that the yoke would be broken within two years, but his death that same year marks his message as false.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast between Hananiah’s words and the chapter’s ending?
